message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code fetches data from a user-supplied URL using requests.get and pd.read_csv without any checksum verification, signature validation, authentication, or content-type enforcement to confirm the integrity or authenticity of the remote source.
No detected label flipping detection: There is no check that validates label values against an expected set, compares label distributions, or uses any label-noise detection tool like Cleanlab.

No detected model integrity verification: The code only trains models from scratch using scikit-learn estimators; no pretrained weights or serialized models are loaded, so no integrity verification (hash check, signature, pinned revision) is implemented or needed, but the control itself is absent.
No detected label distribution validation: There is no code that checks class balance, verifies expected label sets, or detects anomalous label distributions before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: The training loop contains no backdoor defenses such as trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or mechanisms are imported or used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) or stress tests are imported or used anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a train/test split is performed via `create_train_test`, there is no signing, hashing, or isolation mechanism to prevent metric manipulation, and only a single accuracy/score metric is used without independent verification.
No detected output bounds checks: No checks are performed on model prediction outputs for NaN values, probability bounds, or calibrated thresholds before returning results to the user.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The models used are classical ML classifiers/regressors (sklearn), not LLMs, so prompt injection is not applicable, and no such defenses are implemented.
